song_difficulty.notes: IMPORTANT DATA ISSUE: this file is not song lyrics — it is a K-pop comeback/release calendar (dates, artist names, album titles) mistakenly captured as 'lyrics'. It contains no singable Korean lines and should be excluded from the curriculum or re-scraped with the correct lyrics source.
Gentle romantic vocabulary, mostly TOPIK 2-4. Repetitive structure aids learning; retrospective -던 modifier and indirect questions are the main grammar challenges.
Roughly a third of the song is English, which lowers overall difficulty despite some higher-level poetic vocabulary (잔상, 눈동자, 흩어지다).
Narrative storytelling song, mostly beginner-to-intermediate vocabulary with a good variety of common grammar patterns (-(으)면, -(으)ㄹ 거야, -자).
Conversational, dating-themed lyrics with colloquial slang (썸 타다, 차이다). Great for practical spoken-style grammar (-(으)ㄹ래요, -지 마, -아/어서라도).
Gentle, family/love-themed ballad with mostly common vocabulary. Good beginner-to-intermediate song with useful polite endings (-아/어 봐요, -겠죠, -네요).
Heavy English/Korean code-switching with romanization included; Korean portions are relatively short and use common relationship vocabulary, making it approachable despite mixed-language structure.
Upbeat K-pop track with heavy La-la-la filler and English words; Korean lines are short, simple, and repetitive making it approachable despite some level-5 words like 아찔하다.
Simple pop love song; heavy English/Korean code-switching keeps actual Korean vocabulary basic, but switching itself can confuse learners.
Fully Korean, repetitive structure, ideal for beginners; includes useful colloquial contractions like -다매.
Standard ballad vocabulary with several useful intermediate grammar patterns (-ㄹ까 봐, -거라고).
Nostalgic folk-pop with gentle narrative style; entirely Korean, good for intermediate learners.
Mostly English lyrics with a short Korean bridge; low Korean ratio reduces overall exposure despite decent bridge vocabulary.
Fully Korean but short, repetitive, imagery-based lines with simple -고/-면 connectors; romanization included alongside Hangul makes it very approachable.
Fully Korean, short, simple/humorous vocabulary (냄새, 화장실) with only mild grammar variety; easy entry point despite the comedic subject matter.
Fully Korean, casual/conversational break-up-crush lyric with everyday vocabulary; grammar patterns like -다가 보니 and repeated -았다가 -았다가 add some intermediate complexity.

Almost entirely English lyrics with only a handful of short Korean phrases (mostly in the chorus/outro). The Korean present is intermediate (passive verb formation, path/hope imagery) but its low overall volume keeps the song accessible; good for beginners who want light Korean exposure.
Emotional ballad with dense imagery (흔적, 서럽다, 황홀함). Grammar centers on fear/hope constructions (-(으)ㄹ까 봐) and modifiers; a few short English lines break up the Korean.
Reflective, pandemic-themed lyrics with many connective endings (-니까, -듯이, -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다) that reward intermediate learners.
Classic ballad, entirely Korean plus an inline romanization block (useful for pronunciation practice). Solid intermediate vocabulary and a wide range of connective/ending grammar.
Breakup song built around a 'shooting' metaphor; moderate difficulty with useful emotional vocabulary and hoping/quoting grammar (-기를 빌다, -는 거라고).
Nostalgic ballad with inline romanization. Rich variety of past-tense/retrospective grammar (-던, -았/었을 거야, -았/었단 걸) makes it grammar-dense despite simple vocabulary.

Motivational pop-rock lyrics with mostly standard vocabulary; some intermediate abstract verbs (앞지르다, 원망하다, 버티다) push it above beginner level. Some English interjections but core lines are pure Korean.
Mixed Korean/English K-pop chorus; vocabulary skews toward emotional/animal metaphor words (사자, 본능, 길들이다) which are less common. Repetition of hooks helps comprehension despite advanced words.
Playful modern love song with texting-culture vocabulary (이모티콘, 말풍선) and some literary metaphor (은유, 수수께끼); grammar is mostly conversational and approachable.
Iconic ballad with everyday emotional vocabulary and indirect-question grammar (-ㄴ지); accessible but includes some higher-register endings like -(으)ㄴ걸요.
Gentle, poetic, fully Korean ballad; vocabulary is nature/love themed and moderately advanced but sentence patterns are repetitive and singable, aiding learnability.

song_difficulty.safe_name: Jang Beom June - Your Shampoo Scent In The Flowers
song_difficulty.notes: Fully Korean indie ballad about unspoken longing; vocabulary is everyday-level but repeated rhetorical-question grammar (-ㄴ다고 말할까) adds moderate complexity.
Explicit, casual hip-hop/R&B track mixing English and Korean; slang and clipped colloquial speech (다 챙겼음, 숫자 셀게) make it linguistically informal despite moderate vocabulary difficulty.
Confident/sassy tone with modern slang (밀당, 간당간당하다) mixed into otherwise moderate vocabulary.
Flirty, teasing tone with idiomatic phrases (간보다, 내숭 떨다) that add difficulty beyond basic grammar.
Party anthem with brazen/carefree slang (뻔뻔하다) and heavy English mixing.
Reflective overthinking theme with moderate vocabulary; repeated 똑똑 motif aids memorability.
Emotional breakup ballad; entirely Korean, teaches useful -(으)ㄹ게 and -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 patterns.
Catchy pop song with useful hearsay endings (-대, -는대) and moderate-level vocabulary.
Playful dance-pop with colloquial reported-speech endings (-냬, -래) useful for casual speech.

song_difficulty.safe_name: Sogyumo Acacia Band - Almost Blue (2019 Remake)
song_difficulty.notes: Mostly English lyrics with short poetic Korean interludes; the Korean lines that exist use literary endings (-네, -으려네) that are less common for learners.
Idol-pop mixed-language chorus with simple repeated hooks; verses add moderate vocabulary and some useful intermediate grammar (-아/어버리다, -는지 모르다).
Emotional TWICE ballad-pop; English chorus lines are simple but Korean verses use nuanced emotional grammar (-다가도, -고만 싶다, -만 같다) at a slightly higher level than the vocabulary alone suggests.
Playful, colloquial idol song with slang/casual contractions (단걸, 삐지다, 꿀꿀해) and a very large number of grammar patterns packed into short lines.
Repetitive 'I wanna know' English hook makes it feel easy, but Korean verses use reportive/hypothetical structures (-다는데, -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다, -(으)ㄹ는지) that are more advanced than the vocabulary level.
Fully Korean narrative conceit (a phone concert) with a large, concrete vocabulary set (공연, 관객, 통화) but grammar stays mostly at intermediate imperative/request forms.
Fully Korean, introspective lyric with a couple of slang/self-deprecating terms (샌님, 별볼일없다) and consistent, moderately complex indirect-question grammar (-는지, -는데도).

Mostly Korean with heavy line repetition, which aids memorization. Vocabulary centers on body parts and romantic-excitement expressions; grammar uses common casual endings (-(으)ㄹ 거야, -(으)면, -아/어도) plus one idiomatic repeated-past-tense construction. Onomatopoeia (뿜뿜, 쿵쿵) and playful/coy tone push the slang level to medium.
Abstract, metaphor-heavy vocabulary (약점, 완벽하다, 빚다) and layered grammar like -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다 and -길. English chorus lowers the Korean ratio somewhat.
Dense, abstract imagery (구원, 광기, 삼키다) with advanced causative/purpose grammar (-게 해주다, -도록). One of the harder songs in the batch.
Dark, poetic lyrics with dense abstract vocabulary (침묵, 착각, 뒤덮다) and advanced grammar (-(으)ㄹ 테니, -는 날까지). One of the more advanced songs in the batch.
Metaphor-rich (thirst/drink as desire) with the largest vocabulary count in the batch and frequent -듯/-듯한 and -아/어지다 constructions; advanced but not slangy.
Fully Korean ballad with poetic, layered grammar (-아/어서야, -아/어봐도, recollective modifiers) and introspective vocabulary; no slang but demanding sentence structure.
Heavy English gambling/slang vocabulary mixed with intense Korean lines using advanced abstract nouns (강자, 최악, 승리); low overall Korean ratio but the Korean segments are dense and idiomatic.
Literary, metaphor-dense lyrics (수수께끼, 뭉게구름, 간이역) fully in Korean; vocabulary difficulty outweighs grammar complexity, which is fairly plain.

song_difficulty.safe_name: IU, SUGA - eight(Prod.&Feat. SUGA of BTS)
song_difficulty.notes: Emotionally complex duet mixing English hooks with dense Korean verses (SUGA's rap section is especially abstract: 재난문자, 영겁); good mid-high intermediate material.
Poetic, fully Korean love song with archaic/literary endings (-셔요, -ㄹ래) and refined vocabulary (여운, 갈피, 미련); demanding for intermediate learners.
Nostalgic, fully Korean ballad with rich sensory/emotional vocabulary (사무치다, 애틋하다, 시리다) and layered comparative grammar (-(으)ㄴ 듯 그런 듯해); advanced but rewarding.
Fully Korean, metaphor-heavy song about being lost; vocabulary includes many uncommon imagery words (거미줄, 메아리, 뒤엉키다) and obligation grammar (-아/어야만 하다) throughout.
Fashion/trend slang (멘탈, 찌질이, 반사) is advanced despite simple grammar; heavy English chant sections lower overall Korean density.
Introspective breakup ballad, entirely Korean, with dense emotional vocabulary and multiple advanced grammar patterns (-기 마련이다, -나 보다).
Poetic R&B with literary/abstract vocabulary (암전되다, 되뇌다); advanced despite heavy English chorus.
Literary breakup ballad with dense imagery vocabulary (아련하다, 식상하다) and multiple advanced grammar patterns.
Mixed Korean/English (na-na-na hooks) but Korean verses are dense with figurative comparisons (처럼) and varied conditional/past-modifier grammar.
Mostly Korean with a couple of English lines; wide grammar variety (-밖에, -잖아, -고파, -기 전에) packed into a short lyric makes it grammar-dense despite common vocabulary.
Long song heavily code-mixed with English (weekend/plan/surprise), but the Korean portions have the largest vocabulary count in the batch plus advanced constructions like -(으)ㄴ 채 and -는 대로.
Long, conversational, mostly-Korean rap/ballad hybrid with a huge vocabulary load (idioms, retrospective -더라 endings, colloquial contractions) and code-switched English hooks.
OST ballad, almost entirely Korean, with emotionally dense vocabulary (심장, 운명, 눈빛) and a wide range of grammar including continuative -아/어 왔다 and causal -(으)로 인해.
Fully Korean ballad with formal -아요/-ㄹ게요 register, emotionally rich vocabulary (글썽이다, 서글퍼지다), and advanced grammar like -(으)ㄹ까 봐 and -겠지만.

Korean verses use abstract, dreamlike/fantasy imagery (상상하다, 아득히, 이끌다) layered over a heavily English-language hook. Grammar is the main difficulty driver: a wide range of distinct sentence-final endings (-(으)ㄹ래, -(으)ㄹ걸, -더라도, -아야겠다, -든지) appear in a short span, requiring solid intermediate-advanced grammar knowledge.

Confident, boastful lyrics packed with less-common/advanced vocabulary (지겹다, 저지르다, 다채롭다, 변칙, 가뿐하다) and idiomatic casual constructions (될 대로 되라지, -는 게 my motto, -(으)ㄹ 테니). Highest average vocabulary level and vocabulary count in the batch, plus a confrontational slangy tone throughout — the most difficult song of the four.
Boastful rap track packed with slang, idioms, and wordplay (수저, 학을 떼다, 고소하다). Fast, colloquial delivery makes this the most demanding song for listening comprehension.
Rap song mixing archaic/historical vocabulary (뒤주, 종놈, 주리를 틀다), modern slang, and profanity. Recommend a content advisory; likely the hardest and most mature song in the batch.

song_difficulty.notes: Dense, literary rock ballad about growing up; uses many TOPIK 5-6 words (연연하다, 어처구니없다, 무덤덤하다) and complex nominalized/recollective grammar throughout — one of the hardest songs in the batch.
Socially-conscious rap about war and poverty with dense abstract/formal vocabulary and liner-note prose; the most advanced song in the batch.
Entirely Korean, literary/poetic register with advanced vocabulary (담담하다, 노곤하다, 명백하다) and layered modifier/conditional grammar; no English scaffolding to lean on.
